summary:
Phase B review of sub-mv1h2gly-014b868a. I read the code against plan.json's task criteria, the approved design and the brief, and ran every declared verification command myself.

What holds:
- b1, b2, b4 and b3 pass: 171, 110, 9 and 364 tests, and the clean checkout passes (ev:ev-mv1h8qn0-01c0fa75, ev:ev-mv1h94yt-010d769d, ev:ev-mv1h959y-01ee5954, ev:ev-mv1h9yvi-018dc008).
- My independent checks (ev:ev-mv1ha378-01c9beab):
  - the five migrations equal the spec DDL;
  - approvalPageCsp and the app CSP equal the spec strings;
  - package.json scripts equal the spec;
  - the planner matches the brief's RS-06..RS-11 wording exactly;
  - on 3000 random catalogs (807 feasible), the planner agrees with my own brute force written from the brief's rules on best plan, rejections, per-candidate codes and relaxations.
- derive.js matches the revision-2 table row by row, including 2(a)/(b), 3's unknown-refund clause, 4a, 5a and 14. states.js matches the brief's four tables and the OQ-D1 reasons.
- Config, host check, body cap, static confinement, check-node.cjs and the harness meet their criteria.

The blocking defect: my own run of the phase suite failed (ev:ev-mv1h5bbh-010aae6e, 363/364).
- NFR1's 'two processes starting at the same time' test died with SQLITE_BUSY 'database is locked' thrown by `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` in src/db/connection.js, although busy_timeout is set first.
- A reproduction failed 1 of 10 isolated runs (ev:ev-mv1h6fnx-0154466d).
- This is a production race on concurrent start against a fresh database. b1's criterion says such a start is safe, and the later multi-process tests (RS-14, RS-20, RS-26, lease-takeover) depend on it.

Minor findings: six design-item tests lack their id, and two deviations need follow-ups in later tasks. The security reviewer's draft (phase-b-security-1.md) did not exist when I recorded this review.

findings.title: Concurrent start on a fresh database fails: PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL throws SQLITE_BUSY despite busy_timeout
findings.detail:
src/db/connection.js sets `PRAGMA busy_timeout` and then `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` (L29-L30). When several processes open a new database file at the same time, SQLite can return SQLITE_BUSY for the journal-mode switch without calling the busy handler. It does this when waiting could deadlock: one connection holds a shared lock and needs an exclusive one while another holds or waits for a write lock.
- In my phase run of `npm test`, 'NFR1: two processes starting at the same time apply each migration exactly once and both succeed' failed: a child exited with 'Error: database is locked' at openDb, connection.js:30 (ev:ev-mv1h5bbh-010aae6e, 363/364).
- The reproduction ran that test 10 times in isolation; 1 failed with the same error (ev:ev-mv1h6fnx-0154466d).
b1's criterion requires that 'a second process starting at the same time skips applied versions', and the spec calls migrations multi-process safe. The later multi-process tests (rs14, rs20, rs26, lease-takeover, return-crash), and any two-server deployment, start processes on one fresh file and would inherit the race as flaky failures or startup crashes. The delivery lead's 364/364 run and my b1/b3 runs passing does not contradict this: the failure is intermittent.
findings.recommendation:
Owner: b1-foundation-core (backend-engineer), src/db/connection.js.
Fix: openDb retries the journal-mode switch, and any other SQLITE_BUSY raised while opening, with a short bounded back-off up to the busy timeout, then gives a clear error. A synchronous sleep such as Atomics.wait on a SharedArrayBuffer is fine.
Add a regression test (or raise the existing one to at least 25 rounds of 3 processes) named with its id.
Resolved when the reviewer's reruns pass: `npm test` and `node .eccode/drafts/tr-phb-migrate-race.mjs 20` with 0 failures.
If a retry does not remove the failures, dispatch learning-debugger on PB-1 to find the root cause.

findings.recommendation:

findings.title: Deviations that need follow-ups in later tasks
findings.detail:
I accept these deviations, but each creates an obligation the plan does not yet record:
- PlannerLimitError (PLANNER_LIMIT) must not surface as an untyped 500 from POST /api/requests/:id/plan (c2).
- Offers that fail the capacity or cup-diameter match are recorded only in the trace as SPEC_MISMATCH. The request page's 'What was rejected' (RS-35) will not show them, and no design code exists for them (G review, c5/g1).
- The 60 s upload deadline must be enforced in the upload route (d3).
- The seed's embedded RS-FIX-1 is not cross-checked against test/fixtures/rs-fix-1.json: both are only checked against the brief.
- The two AppError classes rely on duck typing in the envelope; that is tested in app.test.js and acceptable.
findings.recommendation:
Owners: c2 (map PLANNER_LIMIT to a catalogued error, e.g. 422 VALIDATION_FAILED, or 503 with a named code added to the catalog through the orchestrator); d3 (upload deadline); c5/g1 (decide with the orchestrator whether SPEC_MISMATCH offers are shown).
Resolved when each item is named in its task's acceptance criteria or handoff. Optionally, b2 adds a test asserting the seed constant equals the fixture file.
